hypothesis: The cart-completion lock keyed by cart id uses the default in-memory locking provider, which only works inside one process. Completing the same cart simultaneously on two servers lets both pass the lock and the order_cart check, creating duplicate orders for one cart and double reservations.

createReservationItems validates each input entry against the level's available quantity individually, without summing entries sharing an inventory item. A cart with OVS-PIECE x6 and OVS-TWOPACK x3 (6 + 6 = 12 units of WIDGET) with stock 10 passes each per-line check but reserves 12 units, overselling.

Reservation inventory locking uses the in-memory lock, process-local. Two different carts for the single SOLO unit, completed on two different servers, both pass availability check and reserve, overselling SOLO or desyncing reserved_quantity.

The reserved_quantity counter is written from a previously read level value, so concurrent reservations on the same level lose an update. Many carts completing together on one WIDGET level should leave reserved_quantity below the sum of reservations.

Reservation level counter is updated from a value read earlier (level.reserved_quantity + adjustment) and the guarding lock is process-local. Many carts completed concurrently across two servers on the same WIDGET level lose counter updates, so reserved_quantity ends below the sum of reservations.

A cart with OVS-TWOPACK x3 (6 units) and OVS-PIECE x5 (5 units) on WIDGET stock 10: each entry fits stock alone but the sum of 11 exceeds it; the per-entry availability check in ensureInventoryLevels never adds entries sharing an item, so the order is created with 11 units reserved.

Stock is lowered after the cart is built, to below the cart's need. Completion should fail on insufficient stock; if availability is read at one location and reserved at another, the order is still created with reservations over stock.
